title: The Future Is Domain-Specific Agents - Justin Schroeder, StandardAgents
talk_summary: Justin Schroeder argues that stacking skills/MCP/tools onto one general agent is 'inheritance' that degrades context and cost, and that composing small domain-specific agents (own system prompt, minimal tools, own loop, own sandbox) coordinated in English is more token-efficient, cheaper, safer, and more parallelizable. He cites ~80% token efficiency and 137x cost gaps between small and large models per task, and predicts token prices rising, making decomposition urgent.

takeaways.technique: Compose narrow sub-agents instead of inflating one agent's context
takeaways.what_they_do: Each capability (Gmail, Figma, travel) is a full agent with its own system prompt, only the tools it needs, and a tiny message history; a coordinator talks to them in plain English.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each of them is a separate isolated agent, a full agent... with its own message history, its own agentic loop
takeaways.numbers: claims over 80% token efficiency for a given task

takeaways.technique: Route narrow tasks to small/cheap models
takeaways.what_they_do: Because a domain agent only does one picked task with minimal context, a small model can execute it faithfully, so you don't need the big model for everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to have the V4 Flash do everything. Instead, it only needs to do the tasks that have been specifically picked for it to do
takeaways.numbers: cites 137x cheaper per task for a small model vs a large one

takeaways.technique: Keep sub-agent context minimal by design
takeaways.what_they_do: The coordinator sends only the specific request ('get that last email from Debbie'); the sub-agent sees just its system message, its tools, and that one message.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that is the totality of the context. It literally just has the system message, its tools, and that message that came in

takeaways.technique: Per-agent sandbox filesystem + code execution as a primitive
takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent gets its own sandboxed file system and code-execution location so it can write and run files without touching the host OS or exfiltrating data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every agent should have a sandboxed code execution location... without interacting with an OS at a higher level. That needs to be baked in as a primitive

takeaways.technique: Capability-limited agents instead of blanket permissions
takeaways.what_they_do: Small domain agents can only do explicitly approved actions, so you stop bypassing permissions for a big do-anything coding agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those agents can't do everything. They can only do the things that are already explicitly approved for them to do

takeaways.technique: Recursive sub-agents for deep domains (compliance, legal)
takeaways.what_they_do: A legal agent spawns a GDPR sub-agent and an OSHA sub-agent so the main agent never carries 45MB of domain context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't want to have 45 megabytes of context just on GDPR. So, we make that a separate sub agent
